title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Array
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on arrays and their properties in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: With each i, the inner loop runs 3 times and WriteLine prints the same value. i=0 gives 0; i=1 gives 4; i=2 gives 8. Console.ReadLine() only pauses between rows; it does not change the printed numbers.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The '++' operator increments the character's Unicode value. 'K' becomes 'L'. 76 is 'L', so B++ becomes 'M'.

questions.question: Complete the following C# code with the missing inner loop so that j is each element of the inner array.
questions.explanation: To iterate through the elements of the inner array 'i', the syntax 'foreach (int j in i)' is used.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: In C#, byte is an unsigned 8-bit type (0 to 255). The cast first truncates 345.09 toward zero to 345, then wraps 345 into the byte range: 345 - 256 = 89.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the following C# code?

options.text: 'a' is a reference to the array created on the stack
'a' is a reference to an object created on the stack
'a' is a reference to an array object whose type is derived from System.Array

questions.explanation: In C#, arrays are reference types allocated on the heap. The array type (here int[]) inherits from System.Array.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using a 2D jagged array over a 2D rectangular array?

options.text: Allows unequal number of elements in each row

questions.explanation: Jagged arrays allow rows to have different lengths, which is useful for sparse data.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the following C# code?

options.text: 'a' represents rectangular array of 2 rows and 3 columns

questions.explanation: int[,] with two nested initializer lists of three values each is a rectangular array of 2 rows and 3 columns. GetUpperBound(0) returns 1 (the last row index), not 2 or 9.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Code runs successfully but prints nothing
The code runs successfully and prints the values

questions.explanation: The params keyword lets display() accept either a comma-separated list of ints (2, 3, 8) or an int array. Both calls are valid and the values are printed.

questions.question: Which is the correct way of defining and initializing an array of 3 integers?
questions.explanation: new int[3]{78, 9, 54} creates an array of length 3. Option a has only two elements. Option b uses a[3], which is out of range (valid indexes are 0..2). Option c is invalid syntax because [] is missing after int.

questions.question: Which of the following is a real difference between declaring an array in C# and in languages such as C?

options.text: In C#, the square brackets come after the type (int[] a), not after the identifier
The array size must be part of the declared type
There is no difference between array declaration in C# and in C

questions.explanation: C# requires int[] name. Unlike C, int name[] is not legal, and the length is not part of the array type, so the same variable can later refer to arrays of different lengths.
